Cyclone Akvan Nears India's East Coast, Evacuations Underway

Severe cyclonic storm Akvan is moving rapidly towards the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coasts, with landfall expected near Gopalpur on November 20. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rain in parts of West Bengal, including Kolkata, and in Jharkhand's Kolhan and southern districts, with an alert for Ranchi. In anticipation of the storm, Odisha has evacuated over 100,000 people from coastal areas, with reports varying between 46,000 and nearly 47,000 evacuated. Red alerts have been issued for 11 districts in Odisha. Over 74 rescue teams, including NDRF and ODRAF, have been deployed. Cyclone Akvan is expected to weaken before landfall, but winds may still reach 110 km/h. The storm has also disrupted train services, with the schedules of 23 trains, including the Vande Bharat, being altered, potentially causing delays of up to 8 hours.
